findings.detail: THE CLASS, not the instances. I may not edit tests/**, so this is the specification for whoever owns it. THE RULE, established by running the real functions over a spelling matrix (not by reading them): a LEVERS READ / WIRES READ block is harvested at all ONLY IF a later line in the same docstring starts (after optional whitespace) with exactly 'LEVERS READ:', 'WIRES READ:' or 'DID IT FIRE:' -- uppercase, colon, no comma; a block that is last, or whose terminator uses a comma, yields NOTHING. Within a harvested block the body is cut at commas that are at paren-depth 0; each piece then has everything from its first '(' to the end deleted (DOTALL, so an unclosed parenthesis is fine and eats the rest of the item), is stripped of whitespace and of leading and trailing '.', and is KEPT only if what remains fullmatches [a-z_][a-z0-9_]*. Consequences a docstring author can follow: (1) a name followed by unparenthesised prose is DESTROYED, including 'name -- note', 'name. Note.', 'name; other', 'name and other'; (2) a name followed by a parenthetical is KEPT ('ctx (only on the refusal path)' -> ctx), and commas inside the parenthetical do not split, so ALL prose belongs inside parentheses; (3) backticks kill an item ('`ctx`' is dropped) and so does any uppercase letter ('CTX' is dropped); (4) 'none' is itself harvested as an item, which is harmless only because no package declares a lever named 'none'; (5) a '#'-continuation line inside a block swallows the name in front of it ('dropout\n# cand_window, foo' keeps only 'foo') -- no instance of this remains in the tree, but the shape is live. SO THE RULE IS: one line, bare lowercase identifiers separated by commas, EVERY word of prose inside parentheses, and never let a READ block be the last block in the docstring. WHAT THE CHECK NEEDS IN ORDER TO FAIL LOUDLY. Today _split_items returns the fragments and stub_reads throws away anything that is not an identifier, silently -- the harvest shrinks and K4 reports the smaller population as fully covered, which is a FALSE PASS by construction, and its detail line ('N named by a stub') cannot distinguish 'nobody declares it' from 'somebody declared it unreadably'. The repair is three additions, none of which relaxes anything: (a) have stub_reads collect the REJECTED items alongside the accepted ones, tagged with package, symbol and block kind; (b) add a check -- call it K15, 'every item in a READ block is harvestable' -- that FAILS on any rejected item and prints it verbatim with its symbol, with the population size printed as every other check here does, so it cannot be vacuous; the only admissible exemption is an item that is empty after stripping (a trailing comma); (c) add a companion assertion that every docstring containing a 'LEVERS READ' or 'WIRES READ' header yields the same number of harvested blocks as raw headers, which is what would have caught src/fabric/api.py::forward's comma. Each wants a selftest() case on a synthetic tree, in the style already used there, since this file's own doctrine is that a check nobody has watched fail is indistinguishable from one that cannot. NOTE THE PRIORITY: with only docstrings fixed, the NEXT bad spelling is silent again.
